disposition_mapping.rationale: Function and actor accountability (FP&A manager as issuer) survive unchanged; the mechanical drafting of the calendar, assumptions and downside scenario is agent-assisted but the manager remains the accountable releaser, per the council's converged draft-then-release pattern. The downside macro scenario (ABB-R-10) is preserved as an explicit, acknowledged input/output, addressing emerging_economy's objection that a global macro feed alone cannot capture multi-rate/capital-controlled realities.

The council decisively rejected merging target-setting into assumption-issuance (maximalist conceded this in Round 2). Four-plus members independently argued that 'unconstrained_by_design' reflects absence of a requirement protecting the artifact, not absence of an accountability boundary: an FP&A-manager-issued assumption and a CEO/CFO-chosen target are different kinds of claims that must remain separately attributable when a miss is investigated. Kept as a distinct step with its original actor and scope.

ABB-R-02 requires survival; the council majority (pragmatist, hitl_designer, emerging_economy, finance_domain, agentic_architect) rejected merging revenue, cost and capex planning into one undifferentiated workspace, holding that ownership of the number is not the same as the tool used to build it. The function persists with the business unit head as accountable submitter, enhanced with agent-assisted first-draft generation and tooling-agnostic, offline-capable entry per emerging_economy's connectivity non-negotiable.

Same reasoning as ABB-03: ABB-R-03 requires survival, the ownership boundary (cost centre owner as accountable preparer) is preserved per the council's rejection of homogenised submission steps, and agent-assisted drafting plus offline-capable, actuals-consistent schema are added as tooling improvements that do not change accountability.

ABB-R-04 requires the carrier to still consume a business case for above-threshold capex; the council (hitl_designer, emerging_economy, finance_domain, agentic_architect all converged) judged that merely consuming the business case as a passive input is insufficient as a control, so an explicit, named CFO/capex-committee review-and-sign-off with documented basis is added inside the step. Business unit heads remain the submitting owner; capex scoring-model replacement was rejected on emerging_economy's non-negotiable that volatile-market capital risk needs a named human judgment.

ABB-R-06 (survival), ABB-R-05 (accounting policies applied to actuals) and ABB-R-07 (central FX assumptions) are satisfied by naming both inputs explicitly on the mechanical roll-up (T6). The council majority (finance_domain, hitl_designer, agentic_architect-conceded, accounting_standards-conceded, emerging_economy-conceded) determined that 'consolidate and reconcile' conflates a genuinely mechanical aggregation with a separate, judgment-heavy reconciliation of circular interest/cash/P&L calculations and intercompany elimination; splitting it into two named activities makes the reconciliation labour visible rather than folding it invisibly inside automation, satisfying KB-02's evidential-trail and KB-05's halt-not-suppress principle. Per pragmatist's condition, both stages retain the same accountable FP&A analyst to avoid a new unmonitored handoff.

The council majority (pragmatist, hitl_designer, finance_domain, agentic_architect, accounting_standards) rejected maximalist's proposal to dissolve review-and-challenge into an exception-only feed of a continuous consolidation engine, on the grounds that exception-flagging alone would never surface judgment calls that don't trip a rule, and that KB-05's error-correction principle requires a logged, inspectable basis for every override, not merely that a meeting occurred. The function survives as a distinct step, bounded into defined rounds with a named escalation path (addressing the genuine calendar-discipline risk pragmatist and finance_domain both identified) and a mandatory override log keyed to the submission it changes.

ABB-R-11 requires survival; every council member treated this as non-negotiable governance with no agent substitution. hitl_designer's addition of a structured decision package (reconciliation status, override log, capex sign-off outcomes, downside-scenario impact) is adopted so approval is an informed judgment rather than a rubber stamp on a summary figure.

ABB-R-09 requires survival and ABB-R-08 requires it to follow board approval, enforced here by T9 preceding T10 and by hard-gating the lock trigger on a verified board-approval artifact. The council split between agentic_architect's fully autonomous lock and the pragmatist/hitl_designer/emerging_economy position requiring a human certification before the lock takes effect; this synthesis sides with the majority view that a correctly-firing trigger answers 'did approval happen' but not 'does the locked artifact equal what the board approved,' while adopting hitl_designer's own proposed middle path (an automated diff presented to a human who must affirmatively release the lock) to avoid reintroducing manual re-keying risk. Emerging_economy's checksummed file-based fallback is preserved as an accepted equivalent where a tier-one platform is unavailable.

steps.description: An assumptions-drafting agent proposes the budget calendar and central planning assumptions (inflation, FX, interest rates) and drafts at least one downside macro scenario from market feeds and prior-year cycle data. The FP&A manager remains the accountable issuer: reviews the draft for local realities (multi-rate FX, capital controls) the global feed may misstate, adjusts, and releases the pack with an acknowledgement-receipt mechanism confirming submitters received and will apply the downside scenario, not only the base case.
steps.name: Issue calendar, central planning assumptions and downside scenario

steps.description: CEO/CFO set top-down revenue, margin and cost targets informed by the strategic plan and the newly issued central assumptions. This remains a distinct, named executive judgment act, kept structurally separate from assumption-issuance so that a later miss can be attributed to either a bad assumption (T1) or a bad target (T2) rather than an undifferentiated process failure. Analytics tooling may supply scenario-achievability comparisons as an aid, but does not set the target.
steps.name: Set top-down targets

steps.description: A drafting agent generates a first-cut revenue/volume projection per business unit from historical trends and pipeline data against the top-down targets and central assumptions. The business unit head reviews, adjusts and owns the final submission as the accountable preparer of record, using tooling-agnostic, offline-capable templates that share the same data schema as cloud-based entry so units with limited connectivity are not structurally disadvantaged.
steps.name: Revenue and volume plans

steps.description: A drafting agent generates a baseline cost/headcount projection from actuals and HR-system data; the cost centre owner reviews, adjusts and owns the submission as the accountable preparer, on the same accrual basis as actuals and via the same tooling-agnostic, offline-capable schema used for revenue planning.
steps.name: Cost centre and headcount budgets

steps.actor: Business unit heads / CFO or capex committee
steps.description: Business unit heads submit capex requests; an agent may assemble the request template and NPV/IRR mechanics, but the business case narrative for requests above the threshold remains human-authored. A CFO or capex committee reviews and signs off on every above-threshold business case before it flows into consolidation, with the approval or rejection and its basis documented, converting the gate from a passively consumed input into an observed decision.
inputs: Business case for capex above threshold
steps.name: Capex requests and business case review

steps.description: A consolidation agent ingests revenue and volume plans, cost centre and headcount budgets, capex requests, the accounting policies applied to actuals, and the central FX assumptions, and mechanically produces a draft three-statement budget prepared on the same accounting basis as actuals, including a parallel roll-up against the downside scenario. All inputs remain explicit, versioned and inspectable rather than embedded constants, so a policy or FX methodology change is visible in the run history.
steps.name: Automated consolidation roll-up

steps.description: The same accountable FP&A analyst who oversees the roll-up reviews its output as a standing responsibility, not merely on exception. This covers the genuinely judgment-heavy work the roll-up cannot mechanize: resolving the circular interest/cash/P&L calculation, applying intercompany elimination judgment, and certifying that the accounting-policy and FX treatment applied matches actuals. Where reconciliation fails or an input is stale or missing, the analyst halts the draft and escalates rather than forcing a tie-out.
steps.name: Three-statement reconciliation and validation

steps.description: The reconciled draft is challenged in a defined, calendared number of structured rounds (a business-unit-level round, then a CFO-level round) with a named escalation path for gaps unresolved at the final round. Variance/anomaly-flagging tooling helps the FP&A manager and CFO triage where to focus challenge, but every change imposed on a submitter's numbers is logged with its basis against the specific submission it alters, so the record shows what was challenged, what changed, and why, not merely that a meeting occurred.
steps.name: Bounded review and challenge rounds

steps.description: The board approves the budget on the basis of a structured decision package: the revised budget, the downside-scenario impact, reconciliation status from T7, the capex business-case sign-off outcomes from T5, and the override/escalation log from T8. This remains an unautomated governance act with no agent in the decision seat.
steps.name: Board approval

steps.description: A load-and-lock mechanism is hard-gated on a verified board-approval artifact and runs an automated, machine-generated diff confirming the system-ready version matches the approved document. A named FP&A analyst reviews that diff and affirmatively certifies the match before the lock takes effect, and the action is written to an immutable, auditable log. Where a tier-one platform is unavailable, a checksummed, version-controlled file-based lock carrying the same immutability guarantee is an accepted equivalent. Any subsequent unlock or rollback requires elevated authorization.
steps.name: Verified load and lock of approved version
